This document contains the analyses used to replicate Vaca et al. (2011). Datasets are pulled from the /CleanData directory, which were produced in the /Scripts/01_Cleaning.Rmd document.

1 All-Cause Mortality

We are going to start by importing our all-cause data and plot the rates by year.

all_cause <- read.csv("../CleanData/all_cause_UCD.csv")
head(all_cause)
##   X year    sex age_group       cod race_eth deaths
## 1 1 1999 female       0-4 all_cause    black    245
## 2 2 1999 female       0-4 all_cause hispanic    703
## 3 3 1999 female       0-4 all_cause    white    446
## 4 4 1999   male       0-4 all_cause    black    266
## 5 5 1999   male       0-4 all_cause hispanic    878
## 6 6 1999   male       0-4 all_cause    white    569
#adding pop data 
dof_data<- read_csv("../CleanData/dof_data_grouped.csv")

#merging
all_cause <- left_join(all_cause,dof_data,
                                by = c("year", "sex", "race_eth", "age_group")) 
head(all_cause) 
##   X year    sex age_group       cod race_eth deaths population
## 1 1 1999 female       0-4 all_cause    black    245   117672.4
## 2 2 1999 female       0-4 all_cause hispanic    703   708958.7
## 3 3 1999 female       0-4 all_cause    white    446   497911.0
## 4 4 1999   male       0-4 all_cause    black    266   121620.5
## 5 5 1999   male       0-4 all_cause hispanic    878   739400.0
## 6 6 1999   male       0-4 all_cause    white    569   526744.7
#making a rate per 100k variable 

all_cause <- all_cause %>% 
  mutate(rate = deaths/(population*100000)) 

#plotting by year 
ggplot(all_cause, aes(year, rate, col= race_eth))+
  facet_wrap(~age_group)+
  geom_line()  

#table of all ages by year, sex, and race/eth
all_cause %>% 
    group_by(race_eth, year, sex) %>%
    summarise(
      deaths = sum(deaths, na.rm=TRUE),
      pop    = sum(population, na.rm=TRUE),
      .groups="drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(rate = deaths/pop*100000)

2 Descriptive Analysis

2.1 Total Death Count

How many deaths occurred over the study period?

all_cause %>% 
  filter(year %in% 2007:2020) %>% 
  summarize(total_deaths = sum(deaths, na.rm = TRUE))
##   total_deaths
## 1      3190417

2.2 Age-adjusted mortality rates

What are the age-adjusted mortality rates for each race/ethnicity group?

#Step 1: keep deaths and population by age group 
data_age <- all_cause %>%
  filter(
    year %in% 2007:2020, 
    !is.na(age_group)
  ) %>%
  group_by(race_eth, age_group) %>%
  summarise(deaths = sum(deaths, na.rm = TRUE),
            pop = sum(population, na.rm = TRUE), 
            .groups="drop")  
head(data_age)
## # A tibble: 6 × 4
##   race_eth age_group deaths      pop
##   <chr>    <chr>      <int>    <dbl>
## 1 black    0-4         4555 2178899.
## 2 black    10-14        426 2036311.
## 3 black    15-19       2068 2306602.
## 4 black    20-24       3743 2378810.
## 5 black    25-29       4053 2318213.
## 6 black    30-34       4426 2159961.
# Step 2: Obtain standard population weight 
dof_data <- read.csv("../CleanData/dof_data_grouped.csv")
std_pop <- dof_data %>%
  filter(
    year == 2000
  ) %>%
  group_by(age_group) %>%
  summarise(std_pop = sum(population), .groups="drop") %>%
  mutate(weight = std_pop / sum(std_pop))

# Step 3: compute age-specific rates
data_age <- data_age %>%
  mutate(rate = deaths / pop)
 
# Step 4: join weights + calculate weighted rates 
adj_rates <- data_age %>%
  left_join(std_pop, by="age_group") %>%
  mutate(weighted_rate = rate * weight)

#sum weighted rates --> age-adjusted rates
table1_adj <- adj_rates %>%
  group_by(race_eth) %>%
  summarise(
    age_adj_rate = sum(weighted_rate) * 100000,
    .groups="drop"
  )
table1_adj
## # A tibble: 3 × 2
##   race_eth age_adj_rate
##   <chr>           <dbl>
## 1 black            853.
## 2 hispanic         535.
## 3 white            639.

3 Table 1

Among males aged 15-24, by race/ethnicity, age-adjusted mortality rates by cause of death.

Steps: 1. subset deaths to males 15-24, years 2007-2020

  1. create a population weighting variable for 2000 to standardize age-adjustments

  2. compute age-specific weights

  3. Join weights to calculate age-adjusted rates

  4. Calculate 95% CIs using log normal approximation to the Poisson distribution

#Step 1: keep deaths and population by age group  
  #Will use the table1 dataframe previously created and add the appropriate populations 
table1 <- read.csv("../CleanData/table1.csv") 
table1 %>% 
  group_by(cod) %>% 
  slice(1:3)

## # Groups:   cod [6]
##    age_group race_eth cod       deaths
##    <chr>     <chr>    <chr>      <int>
##  1 15-19     black    all_cause   1584
##  2 15-19     hispanic all_cause   5755
##  3 15-19     white    all_cause   3159
##  4 15-19     hispanic disease     1239
##  5 20-24     hispanic disease     2087
##  6 15-19     black    disease      267
##  7 15-19     black    homicide     867
##  8 20-24     black    homicide    1405
##  9 15-19     hispanic homicide    1854
## 10 15-19     hispanic injury       536
## 11 20-24     hispanic injury      1388
## 12 15-19     black    injury       120
## 13 15-19     black    mvc          197
## 14 20-24     black    mvc          409
## 15 15-19     hispanic mvc         1407
## 16 15-19     hispanic suicide      620
## 17 20-24     hispanic suicide     1232
## 18 15-19     black    suicide      102
#pulling up population data
pop <- read.csv("../CleanData/dof_data_grouped.csv")  

pop %>%  
  filter(
    sex == "male",
    age_group %in% c("15-19","20-24"),
    year %in% c(2007:2020)
  ) %>% 
  group_by(race_eth) %>% 
  slice(1:3)
## # A tibble: 9 × 5
## # Groups:   race_eth [3]
##   sex   race_eth age_group  year population
##   <chr> <chr>    <chr>     <int>      <dbl>
## 1 male  black    15-19      2007     95139.
## 2 male  black    15-19      2008     96468.
## 3 male  black    15-19      2009     97899.
## 4 male  hispanic 15-19      2007    631868.
## 5 male  hispanic 15-19      2008    650288.
## 6 male  hispanic 15-19      2009    674929.
## 7 male  white    15-19      2007    488891.
## 8 male  white    15-19      2008    480566.
## 9 male  white    15-19      2009    460530.
grouped_pop <- pop %>% 
  filter(
    sex == "male",
    age_group %in% c("15-19","20-24"),
    year %in% c(2007:2020)
  ) %>% 
  group_by(race_eth, age_group) %>% 
  summarize(population = sum(population)) 
head(grouped_pop)
## # A tibble: 6 × 3
## # Groups:   race_eth [3]
##   race_eth age_group population
##   <chr>    <chr>          <dbl>
## 1 black    15-19       1177784.
## 2 black    20-24       1224919.
## 3 hispanic 15-19       9457908.
## 4 hispanic 20-24       9049172.
## 5 white    15-19       5688679.
## 6 white    20-24       6342899.
table1 <- table1 %>% 
  left_join(grouped_pop, by = c("race_eth", "age_group"))
head(table1) 
##   age_group race_eth       cod deaths population
## 1     15-19    black all_cause   1584    1177784
## 2     15-19 hispanic all_cause   5755    9457908
## 3     15-19    white all_cause   3159    5688679
## 4     20-24    black all_cause   2916    1224919
## 5     20-24 hispanic all_cause  10210    9049172
## 6     20-24    white all_cause   7133    6342899
table1 %>%
  filter(cod %in% c("disease", "injury")) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    missing_pop = sum(is.na(population))
  )
##    n missing_pop
## 1 12           0
#Step 2: get standard population weights 
std_pop <- pop %>%
  filter(
    year == 2000,
    age_group %in% c("15-19","20-24"),
    sex == "male"
  ) %>%
  group_by(age_group) %>%
  summarise(std_pop = sum(population), .groups="drop") %>%
  mutate(weight = std_pop / sum(std_pop))

# Step 3: compute age-specific rates
table1 <- table1 %>%
  mutate(rate = deaths / population)
table1 %>% 
  group_by(cod) %>% 
  slice(1:3)
## # A tibble: 18 × 6
## # Groups:   cod [6]
##    age_group race_eth cod       deaths population      rate
##    <chr>     <chr>    <chr>      <int>      <dbl>     <dbl>
##  1 15-19     black    all_cause   1584   1177784. 0.00134  
##  2 15-19     hispanic all_cause   5755   9457908. 0.000608 
##  3 15-19     white    all_cause   3159   5688679. 0.000555 
##  4 15-19     hispanic disease     1239   9457908. 0.000131 
##  5 20-24     hispanic disease     2087   9049172. 0.000231 
##  6 15-19     black    disease      267   1177784. 0.000227 
##  7 15-19     black    homicide     867   1177784. 0.000736 
##  8 20-24     black    homicide    1405   1224919. 0.00115  
##  9 15-19     hispanic homicide    1854   9457908. 0.000196 
## 10 15-19     hispanic injury       536   9457908. 0.0000567
## 11 20-24     hispanic injury      1388   9049172. 0.000153 
## 12 15-19     black    injury       120   1177784. 0.000102 
## 13 15-19     black    mvc          197   1177784. 0.000167 
## 14 20-24     black    mvc          409   1224919. 0.000334 
## 15 15-19     hispanic mvc         1407   9457908. 0.000149 
## 16 15-19     hispanic suicide      620   9457908. 0.0000656
## 17 20-24     hispanic suicide     1232   9049172. 0.000136 
## 18 15-19     black    suicide      102   1177784. 0.0000866
# Step 4: join weights + calculate weighted rates 
adj_rates <- table1 %>%
  left_join(std_pop, by="age_group") %>%
  mutate(weighted_rate = rate * weight) 

#sum weighted rates --> age-adjusted rates
n_years <- 14

table1_adj <- adj_rates %>%
  group_by(race_eth, cod) %>%
  summarise(
    adj_rate = sum(weighted_rate) / n_years,
    deaths_total = sum(deaths),
    .groups="drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    rate_100k = adj_rate * 100000,
    se_log = 1 / sqrt(deaths_total),
    lcl = rate_100k * exp(-1.96 * se_log),
    ucl = rate_100k * exp( 1.96 * se_log)
  ) 

table1_adj %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .by = c(cod, race_eth)) %>%
  filter(n > 1)
## # A tibble: 0 × 3
## # ℹ 3 variables: cod <chr>, race_eth <chr>, n <int>
# Step 5: adding poisson CI 
table1_adj <- adj_rates %>%
  group_by(race_eth, cod) %>%
  summarise(
    adj_rate = sum(weighted_rate),
    deaths_total = sum(deaths),
    .groups="drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    rate_100k = adj_rate * 100000,

    se_log = 1 / sqrt(deaths_total),

    lcl = rate_100k * exp(-1.96 * se_log),
    ucl = rate_100k * exp( 1.96 * se_log)
  )

#formatting
table1_adj <- table1_adj %>%
  mutate(
    rate_ci = sprintf(
      "%.1f (%.1f–%.1f)",
      rate_100k, lcl, ucl
    )
  ) 

table1_adj %>% 
  group_by(cod) %>% 
  slice(1:3)

Formatting table 1:

cod_levels <- c(
  "homicide",
  "mvc",
  "suicide",
  "injury",
  "disease",
  "all_cause"
)

cod_labels <- c(
  homicide = "Homicide",
  mvc = "Motor Vehicle Crashes",
  suicide = "Suicide",
  injury = "Other Injuries",
  disease = "Other Disease",
  all_cause = "Total (All Causes)"
) 

table1_final <- table1_adj %>%
  mutate(
    cod = factor(cod, levels = cod_levels, ordered = TRUE),
    cod = recode(cod, !!!cod_labels)
  ) %>%
  arrange(cod)


table1_wide <- table1_final %>%
  select(cod, race_eth, rate_ci) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = race_eth,
    values_from = rate_ci
  ) %>%
  arrange(cod)

knitr::kable(
  table1_wide,
  caption = "Table 1. Annual mortality rates (95% CI) per 100,000 by cause of death and race/ethnic group. California males age 15–24 years, 2007–2020."
)

4 All Cause

4.1 Fig 1- Male

Male all-cause mortality rate ratios comparing Hispanic and non-Hispanic black mortality to non-Hispanic white mortality, by 5 year age groups with 95% CI, California, 2007-2020.

yrs_0720 <- 2007:2020
fig1 <- calc_rates(all_cause,yrs_0720,"male","all_cause") %>%
  calc_rr() 

plot_rr(fig1,NULL) 

fig1_plot <- plot_rr(fig1, NULL)
ggsave(
  filename = "../Output/fig1UCD.png",
  plot = fig1_plot,
  width = 10,
  height = 6
)

#trying again, this time for the other years 
yrs_9906 <-c(1999:2006)
fig1_old <- calc_rates(all_cause,yrs_9906,"male","all_cause") %>%
  calc_rr() 
 plot_rr(fig1_old,NULL)

  arrange(race_eth, age_group) %>%
  group_split(race_eth)

4.2 Fig 2- Female

Female all cause mortality rate ratios comparing Hispanic and non-Hispanic black mortality to non-Hispanic white mortality, by 5 year age groups with 95% CI, California, 2007-2020.

fig2 <- all_cause %>%
  calc_rates(yrs_0720,"female","all_cause") %>%
  calc_rr() 

fig2 <- fig2 %>% 
   filter(!(race_eth == "black" & age_group == "5-9")) 


plot_rr(fig2, NULL)

fig2_plot <- plot_rr(fig2, NULL)
ggsave(
  filename = "../Output/fig2UCD.png",
  plot = fig2_plot,
  width = 10,
  height = 6
)

There is a slight problem here, because we are missing the 5-9 counts for Blacks most of the years due to data suppression. Because of this, we will eventually need to exclude this group.

Looking through the numbers:

tables_by_race <- fig2 %>%
  mutate(rr_ci = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f, %.2f)", rr, rr_lcl, rr_ucl)) %>%
  select(race_eth, age_group, rr_ci) %>%
  arrange(race_eth, age_group) %>%
  group_split(race_eth)

names(tables_by_race) <- unique(fig1$race_eth)

5 Homicide

We will pull two cleaned datasets for this, including the homicide counts by age group for the whole study period, and the homicide counts by year.

5.1 Fig 3- Male

Male homicide mortality rates, comparing Hispanic, non-Hispanic black, and non-Latino white, 5 year age groups, California 2007-2020.

hom_age <- read.csv("../CleanData/homicide_UCD_age_groups.csv")
head(hom_age) 
##   X race_eth age_group      cod deaths population
## 1 1    black       0-4 homicide     91    1104550
## 2 2    black     10-14 homicide     37    1031841
## 3 3    black     15-19 homicide    867    1177784
## 4 4    black     20-24 homicide   1405    1224919
## 5 5    black     25-29 homicide   1134    1196638
## 6 6    black     30-34 homicide    874    1105255
fig3 <- hom_age %>%
    mutate(rate = deaths/population*100000) %>%
    set_age_order() %>% 
   rowwise() %>%
  mutate(ci_exact(deaths,population)) %>%
  ungroup()

plot_rate(fig3,NULL) 

fig3_plot <- plot_rate(fig3, NULL, legend_pos = c(.8,.8))
ggsave(
  filename = "../Output/fig3UCD.png",
  plot = fig3_plot,
  width = 10,
  height = 6
)

By number:

tables_by_race <- fig3 %>%
  mutate(r_ci = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f, %.2f)", rate, lcl, ucl)) %>%
  select(race_eth, age_group, r_ci) %>%
  arrange(race_eth, age_group) %>%
  group_split(race_eth)

names(tables_by_race) <- unique(fig3$race_eth)

6 All cause minus homicide

6.1 Figure 4: Male mortality rate ratios

Male mortality rate ratios for all causes except homicide, comparing Hispanic and non-Hispanic black mortality to non-Hispanic white mortality, by 5 year age groups with 95% CI, California, 2007-2020.

all_cause_age <- all_cause %>% 
  group_by(race_eth, age_group) %>%
    summarise(
      deaths = sum(deaths, na.rm=TRUE),
      pop    = sum(population, na.rm=TRUE)
    )
fig4 <- full_join(all_cause_age,hom_age, by = c("race_eth", "age_group")) %>%
  rename(all_cause = deaths.x,
         homicide = deaths.y) %>% 
  mutate(deaths=all_cause-homicide,
         rate=deaths/pop*100000) %>%
  set_age_order() %>%
  calc_rr()

plot_rr(fig4,NULL) 

#do we not have homicide deaths for 0-4? 
hom_age %>% 
  filter(race_eth == "black",
         age_group == "0-4")
##   X race_eth age_group      cod deaths population
## 1 1    black       0-4 homicide     91    1104550
all_cause_age %>% 
   filter(race_eth == "black",
         age_group == "0-4")
## # A tibble: 1 × 4
## # Groups:   race_eth [1]
##   race_eth age_group deaths      pop
##   <chr>    <chr>      <int>    <dbl>
## 1 black    0-4         8291 3682975.
fig4_plot <- plot_rr(fig4,NULL)  
ggsave(
  filename = "../Output/fig4UCD.png",
  plot = fig4_plot,
  width = 10,
  height = 6
)

7 Motor vehicle

7.1 Figure 6: Male by age

Male motor vehicle crash mortality rates, comparing Hispanic, non-Hispanic black, and non-Hispanic white, 5 year age groups with 95% CI, California 2007-2020. We start by following the same methods as before, but run into an issue with missing data due to the CDC query suppression rules. We cleaned a unique dataset with the information needed for this specifically, which we will use.

mvc_age <- read.csv("../CleanData/mvc_UCD_age.csv")
fig6 <- mvc_age %>%
  mutate(rate = deaths/population*100000) %>%
  set_age_order() %>% 
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(ci_log(rate,deaths)) %>%
ungroup()
 
head(fig6) 
## # A tibble: 6 × 9
##       X race_eth age_group cod   deaths population  rate   lcl   ucl
##   <int> <chr>    <ord>     <chr>  <int>      <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
## 1     1 black    0-4       mvc       34   1104550.  3.08  2.20  4.31
## 2     2 black    10-14     mvc       46   1031841.  4.46  3.34  5.95
## 3     3 black    15-19     mvc      197   1177784. 16.7  14.5  19.2 
## 4     4 black    20-24     mvc      409   1224919. 33.4  30.3  36.8 
## 5     5 black    25-29     mvc      417   1196638. 34.8  31.7  38.4 
## 6     6 black    30-34     mvc      303   1105255. 27.4  24.5  30.7
fig6 <- fig6 %>% 
  filter(!(race_eth == "black" & age_group == "90+"))

plot_rate(fig6, NULL, legend_pos = c(0.75,0.82))  

fig6_plot <- plot_rate(fig6, NULL, legend_pos = c(0.75,0.82))   

ggsave(
  filename = "../Output/fig6UCD.png",
  plot = fig6_plot,
  width = 11,
  height = 7
)

One thing important to note is that we are missing data for 90+ due to data suppression for Non-Hispanic Blacks, so we will exclude that from the plot and data.

  select(race_eth, age_group, r_ci) %>%
  arrange(race_eth, age_group) %>%
  group_split(race_eth)

7.2 Figure 7: Male by year (15-24)

Motor vehicle mortality rates, among males 15-24 years of age, comparing Hispanic, non-Hispanic black, and non-Hispanic white, by year with 95% CI, California 2007-2020.

yearly_mvc <- read.csv("../CleanData/mvc_UCD_yearly.csv")

fig7 <- yearly_mvc%>%
  mutate(rate=deaths/population*100000) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(ci_exact(deaths,population)) %>%
  ungroup()

plot_yearly(fig7, NULL) 

fig7_plot <- plot_yearly(fig7, NULL, legend_pos = c(0.8,0.85)) 
ggsave(
  filename = "../Output/fig7UCD.png",
  plot = fig7_plot,
  width = 11,
  height = 7
)
table7 <- fig7 %>%
  mutate(r_ci = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f, %.2f)", rate, lcl, ucl)) %>%
  select(race_eth, year, r_ci) %>%
  arrange(race_eth, year) %>%
  group_split(race_eth)

names(table7) <- unique(fig7$race_eth)

table7
